title: The canonical base-change mate is identity on an open isomorphism locus
statement:
Fix a prime $\ell$ and a field $k$ of characteristic $p>0$ with $p\ne\ell$, and use separated finite-type $k$-schemes and $k$-morphisms [sk-def-sfb-dc-setting]. Let $\Lambda$ be an admissible commutative condensed coefficient of [sk-def-localizing-closure]. For each scheme $T$ use the ordinary unbounded module-object derived category $D(\Mod_{\Lambda_T})$ and the canonical adjunction $a^*\dashv Ra_*$ of [sk-def-sfb-module-derived-pushpull]; pullback is exact by [sk-prop-sfb-cartesian-coefficients]. Let $h:D\to Z$ be a morphism and $j:U\hookrightarrow Z$ a quasi-compact open immersion [def-weil-open-immersion, def-weil-finite-type-morphism]. Specify an identification $h^{-1}(U)\cong U$ under which $h|_{h^{-1}(U)}$ is $\mathrm{id}_U$, and let $i:U\hookrightarrow D$ be the resulting open inclusion. No properness or density hypothesis is imposed on $h$.

Let $v:Z'\to Z$ be any morphism in the setting. Put $D'=D\times_ZZ'$, $h':D'\to Z'$, $w:D'\to D$, $U'=U\times_ZZ'$, $v_U:U'\to U$, and let $j':U'\hookrightarrow Z'$, $i':U'\hookrightarrow D'$ be the open maps. The square $(h,h',v,w)$ is Cartesian [def-weil-pbc-cartesian-square]. Let $\theta:h'^*v^*\xrightarrow{\sim}w^*h^*$ be the comparison induced termwise by module pullback composition [def-sfb-module-upper-star-comp]. Define its derived mate [def-weil-pbc-adjunction-mate] by
$$B_{h,K}=Rh'_*(w^*\varepsilon_{h,K})\circ Rh'_*(\theta_{Rh_*K})\circ\eta_{h',v^*Rh_*K}:v^*Rh_*K\longrightarrow Rh'_*w^*K.$$
There are canonical natural restriction isomorphisms $r_h:j^*Rh_*\xrightarrow{\sim}i^*$ and $r_{h'}:j'^*Rh'_*\xrightarrow{\sim}i'^*$, induced by the underived section identity $(h_*M)(V\to U)=M(V\to U\xrightarrow{i}D)$ and its primed version, using K-injective resolutions. Under these isomorphisms and the canonical pullback compositions $j'^*v^*\cong v_U^*j^*$ and $i'^*w^*\cong v_U^*i^*$, one has
$$j'^*B_{h,K}=\mathrm{id}_{v_U^*i^*K}$$
for every $K\in D(\Mod_{\Lambda_D})$, naturally in $K$. This asserts equality of the specified derived morphisms, without asserting that $B_{h,K}$ is an isomorphism before restriction.

proof.text: Work with the small site representatives in the coefficient universe. By [lem-weil-proetale-weakly-etale-localization](1), the sites over the open $U$ are the slice sites at $j$ and $i$. By [lem-sfb-internal-module-operations-transport], internal module objects, their pullbacks, direct images and specified adjunctions identify with sectionwise modules over the reconstructed coefficient ring sheaves, including the units and counits. This exact equivalence preserves K-injectivity: it identifies the Hom groups from acyclic complexes, which define K-injectivity. We may therefore calculate with ringed-site modules and carry back the resulting morphisms. By [sk-prop-sfb-cartesian-coefficients](1), each coefficient comparison is an isomorphism and every module pullback in the diagram is exact and additive. Thus its derived functor is the termwise functor. The Cartesian identification gives $D'\times_{Z'}U'=h^{-1}(U)\times_UU'=U'$, with $h'|_{U'}=\mathrm{id}_{U'}$. All the following constructions apply to the primed and unprimed triples.

source.place: lemma-localize-morphism-ringed-sites; module-object transport and Cartesian coefficients as in the cited blueprint nodes

proof.text: At the sheaf level write $c_h:j^*h_*\xrightarrow{\sim}i^*$ for the sectionwise identification. Indeed, for every pro-etale $T\to U$, $T\times_ZD=T$ by the specified identification $h^{-1}(U)=U$, so both sides evaluate to $M(T\to U\xrightarrow{i}D)$ by [def-sfb-finite-lower-star] and [def-pur-localized-ringed-site]. Their restriction maps coincide. Their module actions coincide as well: [def-sfb-module-lower-star] uses the structural ring map, whose restriction along the identity $U\to U$ is the identity. Let $a_h:i^*h^*\xrightarrow{\sim}j^*$ be the pullback-composition comparison for $h i=j$ from [def-sfb-module-upper-star-comp], followed by the specified equality. On the localized sites this is the usual identity-pullback identification, with tensor unit $1\otimes m\mapsto m$: its right-adjoint comparison is the sectionwise composition identification of [def-sfb-module-lower-star-comp], so the defining conjugacy gives this normalization. Define $c_{h'}$ and $a_{h'}$ in exactly these ways for $h'i'=j'$.

source.place: lemma-localize-morphism-ringed-sites, sectionwise identities, specialized to identity localized vertical map

proof.text:
These underived comparisons respect adjuncts. In fact, for a section $s\in M(T\to U\xrightarrow{j}Z)$ the unit of the canonical module adjunction sends $s$ to the universal pullback section $1\otimes s$. On the localized identity morphism, $a_{h,M}$ sends that section back to $s$. Consequently $c_{h,h^*M}\,j^*(\eta_{h,M})=a_{h,M}^{-1}$ on every site object, hence as module-sheaf maps. This uses the concrete tensor/adjunction bijection in [def-sfb-module-upper-lower-adjunction] and its preservation by [lem-sfb-internal-module-operations-transport]. For any $t:h^*M\to N$, write $t^\sharp=h_*t\circ\eta_{h,M}$. Naturality of $c_h$ gives
$$c_{h,N}\,j^*(t^\sharp)=i^*(t)\,c_{h,h^*M}\,j^*(\eta_{h,M})=i^*(t)\,a_{h,M}^{-1}.$$
This is precisely the adjunct compatibility with the identity adjunction on $U$. The same section calculation with $T\to U'$ proves the primed compatibility.

source.place: lemma-localize-morphism-ringed-sites; calculation of the localized module-adjunction unit

proof.text:
Choose a K-injective resolution $K\to I$ in the sectionwise module category using [prop-pur-kinjective-resolutions-exist], and use the exact equivalence of step 1 for internal modules. By [sk-def-sfb-module-derived-pushpull], $h_*I$ represents $Rh_*K$. The complex $i^*I$ is K-injective on the slice by [lem-pur-kinjective-restrict-localized]; $K\to I$ restricts to a quasi-isomorphism because restriction is exact. The degreewise section identity $c_{h,I}:j^*h_*I\cong i^*I$ therefore yields
$$r_{h,K}:j^*Rh_*K\xrightarrow{\sim}i^*K.$$
This is exactly the K-injective normalization in the statement. On complexes the maps $c_{h,I}$ are natural, and the canonical resolution comparisons are natural by the right-derived construction [def-sfb-right-derived-functor], so $r_h$ is a natural isomorphism. Repeating this argument for $h'$ gives $r_{h'}$; there is no assumption that $w^*I$ is K-injective.

Check the right-derived-functor hypothesis needed to transport adjuncts. The underived functor $j^*h_*$ is naturally isomorphic via $c_h$ to the exact functor $i^*$. Its termwise derived factorization is consequently its total right derived functor by [lem-weil-pbc-exact-functor-derived-functor](1). The natural isomorphism $r_h$ of step 4 identifies that factorization with $j^*Rh_*$. It also identifies their comparison units: if $P\to I$ is a resolution, naturality of $c_h$ says
$$c_{h,I}\circ j^*h_*(P\to I)=i^*(P\to I)\circ c_{h,P}.$$
After localization, the right-hand resolution map is invertible and is exactly the one used to identify $i^*I$ with $i^*P$. Thus $r_{h,QP}\,j^*(\gamma_{h,P})=Q(c_{h,P})$, with $\gamma$ the right-derived comparison unit of [def-sfb-right-derived-functor]. Hence $j^*Rh_*$, with its localized comparison unit, is a right derived functor of $j^*h_*$. The identical argument proves this assertion for $h'$.

source.place: lemma-restrict-direct-image-open, proof; exact-functor derived universal property applied to the sectionwise identification

proof.text:
Apply [lem-kun-derived-adjoint-square-comparison] with
$$(L,R,V,W)=(h^*,h_*,i^*,j^*),\qquad L_0=R_0=\mathrm{id}_{\Mod_{\Lambda_U}},\quad (a,c)=(a_h,c_h).$$
The identity adjunction has identity unit and counit [def-weil-pbc-composite-adjunction]. All four functors required to be exact are exact by step 1; the underived adjunct condition was verified in step 3, the total derived adjunction exists by [sk-def-sfb-module-derived-pushpull], and the extra right-derived hypothesis and normalization $b=r_h$ were verified in step 5. Its two formulas consequently give, now on the derived categories,
$$r_{h,h^*A}\circ j^*(\eta_{h,A})=a_{h,A}^{-1},\qquad i^*(\varepsilon_{h,K})=r_{h,K}\circ a_{h,Rh_*K}.$$
Apply the same theorem to $(h'^*,h'_*,i'^*,j'^*)$ to obtain these formulas with primes. Here and below $a_h$ also denotes its termwise derived comparison, as required by the theorem; no other derived adjunction or arbitrary isomorphism of functors is substituted.

source.place: Tag 09T5, lemma-derived-adjoint-functors; exact adjoint-square specialization supplied by the cited node

proof.text:
Put $s:j'^*v^*\xrightarrow{\sim}v_U^*j^*$ and $t:i'^*w^*\xrightarrow{\sim}v_U^*i^*$. The comparison $\theta$ and these two comparisons all use [def-sfb-module-upper-star-comp]. The composite Hom bijection is the composite of the two Hom bijections [def-weil-pbc-composite-adjunction]. Their associativity follows directly from that definition and the comparison normalization: the conjugate of either reassociation is the same sectionwise composition map of pushforwards in [def-sfb-module-lower-star-comp], and conjugation is injective and respects composition [def-weil-pbc-adjunction-conjugate]. Inserting the identity localized map $h|_U=h'|_{U'}=\mathrm{id}$, the two reassociations of pullback along the equality $hwi'=vj'=jv_U$ therefore give
$$t_{h^*A}\circ i'^*(\theta_A)\circ a_{h',v^*A}^{-1}
 =v_U^*(a_{h,A}^{-1})\circ s_A.$$
To check the normalization, before deriving, both right-adjoint composites evaluate a sheaf on the very same iterated fibre product; the associativity map sends a tuple of projections to that tuple. Their composites to the final fibre product agree by its universal property, so the section maps agree, not merely up to an unspecified automorphism. This proves the displayed comparison identity on sheaves, and all pullbacks are exact, so the same equality holds termwise on complexes and on their derived categories.

split_report.blueprint: Realizes det-sf-comp-composition-base-change proof (3), the sentence that proper base change for h is compatible with restriction to the open X′ on which h′ is the identity. The calculation needs neither properness nor density once h^{-1}(U)=U is specified.

tool_uses.why: Identifies the pro-etale open sites with slice sites, allowing the ringed-site K-injective restriction theorem; this is a localization tool, not a new compactification route.
Identifies internal condensed modules with ringed-site modules and preserves their specified adjunction units and counits, rather than only their underlying categories.
Supplies exact module pullback for all admissible condensed coefficients; exactness is required by the derived adjoint-square theorem.
Supplies unbounded K-injective resolutions on the chosen small ringed sites; no compactification-specific result replaces this existence tool.
Supplies K-injectivity after open slice restriction, with arbitrary ring sheaves and unbounded complexes.
Identifies the derived exact restriction functor with its total right derived functor, verifying the extra hypothesis of the derived square comparison.
Supplies preservation of adjuncts, units and counits by a canonical right-derived square comparison after all its hypotheses are checked; the composition unit has no such generic categorical theorem.
Specifies the unbounded total module derived functors and their canonical adjunction, rather than a completed or bounded substitute.
